objects.summary: P2 B2 review finds dataset metadata is never validated, so altered/missing meta.json can still yield NEGATIVE_REPLICATION_CONFIRMED despite preregistration requiring provenance/PIT metadata to match. Metadata identity must be part of the input gate.
Builder confirms B4 multiplicity-source conflict fix in 7ed3c7f808: registry and STATE are both checked when present; disagreement now yields INVALID_TRIAL_COUNT with dedicated tests.

Builder does not rerun already-spent B2; instead performs post-hoc evidence check showing meta.json unchanged since ingestion, matching fingerprint/range/validation. B2 result is retained while missing harness gate is acknowledged and added to B4.

P2 B4 review finds iterative tolerance tie-break can choose a later lookback through a chain of near-ties even though preregistration requires the smallest lookback within tolerance of the global maximum. Selection must compute max first, then choose minimum eligible L.

P2 B4 review finds post-write repository mutation returns rc=3 but leaves an already-written JSON claiming the old valid RESULT/return_code. Persistent artifact must be removed or rewritten invalid before exit so disk evidence cannot contradict process failure.

cross_object_findings.finding: A stable CSV hash alone is insufficient when preregistration relies on metadata for dataset identity, date range, validation and PIT properties; metadata must be bound and checked too.

When a single-use run omitted a gate but independent primary evidence proves the actual input metadata was unchanged and valid, the control deficiency can be recorded and corrected prospectively without consuming the outcome again.
Numerically small selection differences can change the chosen specification; preregistered tie rules must be implemented against the global maximum rather than path-dependent iterative comparisons.
If a late integrity check fails after result serialization, the durable artifact must reflect failure; exit code alone is not enough because future readers may only see the JSON.
